newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian activists protest against Israel fair.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian activists protest against Israel fair.

text.p: Scores of riot police blocked about 1,000 Jordanian protesters trying to reach the site of the first Israeli trade fair in Amman hours before it was due to open on Wednesday, witnesses said.
But the demonstration and security measures forced organisers to delay the opening of the exhibition by a few hours.

Police formed three human chains to seal off the main street leading to the fair and shoved away scores of the anti-Israeli demonstrators who were chanting Islam's rallying cry of "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest) and "Jordan's land is Arab not Zionist".
An armoured police vehicle splashed coloured water over some protesters, but no clashes between demonstrators and police were reported, the witnesses said.

Former prime minister and intelligence chief Ahmed Obeidat, who led the campaign, urged calm, telling the protesters that "the security forces are brother Jordanians like us...their feelings are like ours and they are only given orders".
"Our aim is the security of Jordan...The insistence of the authorities to allow this exhibition to take place is damaging Jordan's security by allowing Israel to penetrate us," Obeidat told Reuters.
The demonstation was organised by a national committee that represents a broad-based coalition of parties and unions that has vowed to disrupt by peaceful protest the exhibition.
The grouping reflects the strength of anti-Israeli feelings among many Jordanians who still shun contacts despite the 1994 peace treaty that ended a 46-year state of war.
"Normalisation is a Jewish weapon that threatens our national unity," said a banner hoisted by the Moslem Brotherhood. Another read: "The Israeli industries exhibition is a danger, stop it."
The official opening of the fair by the Israeli ambassador in Jordan was delayed for few hours to later in the day because of problems posed by the security measures, organisers said.
Seventy Israeli companies have booked display space on the exhibition's site with 200 Israeli businessmen expected to attend.
